steps: Delete leading and trailing spaces, tabs, and line breaks, and reduce every internal run of whitespace to one ordinary space (5.1).
Leave an empty field empty and do not insert any substitute value (5.2).
Replace a complete value matching a listed not-applicable entry, regardless of capitalization, with N/A and stop processing that value (5.3).
Replace a complete value matching a listed pending entry, regardless of capitalization, with TBA and stop processing that value (5.4).
Delete a leading attribute name followed by a colon, equals sign, or space before applying attribute-specific rules (5.5).

Compare the received value with recognized variants and prescribed forms while disregarding differences in capitalization, spaces, hyphens, underscores, and full stops, and adopt the prescribed form when a match is found (5.8).

If no match is found, interchange the two parts of a single-comma descriptive value when permitted, omit the comma, and compare again, but never rearrange designations governed by Clauses 8 and 9 (5.9).
Apply the rules governing the attribute, including its numerical presentation, accepted units, unit conversion, designations, and recognized variants (4.3, 7.1-7.3).
Convert only units accepted for the attribute, round converted results half up to the specified number of decimal places, and do not round values already received in the prescribed unit (7.2-7.3).
Delete trailing zeros from the decimal part and delete the decimal point when no decimal digit remains, while writing a leading zero before the decimal point for magnitudes below one (6.4).
Use a full stop as the only decimal separator, delete thousands separators, and apply the prescribed sign, unit spacing, range, tolerance, and dimension formatting rules (6.4, 6.6, 6.10, 6.12-6.13).
Apply the prescribed capitalization and punctuation last, retaining capitals in abbreviations, codes, chemical formulas, and proper names (4.3, 5.6-5.7).

Leave a value unchanged and enter it in the query register when it is ambiguous, contains unresolved alternatives, uses an unaccepted unit, lacks a required unit, cannot be matched after permitted rearrangement, or would lose information if presented (4.4, 6.8-6.9, A.1).
Do not make assumptions, infer meanings, correct spelling, substitute a nearby recognized variant, divide or combine values, or transfer information between attributes (A.1).

Take tag numbers, serial numbers, manufacturers' model numbers and type codes, manufacturers' names, document and certificate numbers, dates, free-text remarks, and attributes outside this standard as received, subject only to whitespace processing (20.1-20.2).
unclear: The mapping of a supplier or contractor's different attribute name to the standard attribute name is outside the scope of the standard (1.2).
An apparent conflict between a general clause and a supplementary attribute clause must be referred to the data owner rather than resolved by the user (4.2).
Values requiring an engineering decision must be referred to the responsible discipline (A.3).
